e-3065.knowledge_point: Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length Given Its Arc Length
e-3065.problem: Consider the curve  $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle 2t-1 ,\: 8t+2 ,\: -2t \right\rangle, \, t \geq 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $\mathbf{r}(0)$ to $\mathbf{r}(t)$ is given by $s=6\sqrt{2}t.$ Find $\mathbf R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
e-3065.worked_solution:
First, since  $s=6\sqrt{2}t,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}6\sqrt{2}t & =s \\ t & =\frac{s}{6\sqrt{2}} \\ t & =\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ by its arc length $s,$ with $s \geq 0,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12}) \\  & =⟨2(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12})-1,\,8(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12})+2,\,-2(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{6}-1,\,\frac{4\sqrt{2}s}{6}+2,\,-\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{6}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨\sqrt{2}s-6,\,4\sqrt{2}s+12,\,-\sqrt{2}s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

e-3067.knowledge_point: Finding a Unit Tangent Given the Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length
e-3067.problem: Given the curve  $\mathbf r(t)=\cos{t}\,\mathbf i - \sin{t}\,\mathbf j+\sqrt{3}t\,\mathbf k, \, t \geq 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $\mathbf r(0)$ to $\mathbf r(t)$ is given by $s=2t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $\mathbf{T}(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
e-3067.worked_solution:
First, since $s=2t,$ we have that $t=\dfrac{s}{2}.$

Therefore, the vector function $\mathbf R(s)$ that parametrizes $\mathbf r(t)$ by its arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{s}{2}k \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}s}{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s,$ the unit tangent can be found as

$$
\mathbf T(s) = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}s}\mathbf R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{3}s}{2})k \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\sqrt{3}\,k).\end{aligned}
$$

e-3066.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length
e-3066.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve  $\mathbf r(t)=2(t\cos{t}-\sin{t})\,\mathbf i+2(t\sin{t}+\cos{t})\,\mathbf j, \, t \geq 0$ by its arc length $s?$
e-3066.worked_solution:
First, we find $\mathbf{r}'(t)$ and its magnitude $\|\mathbf{r}'(t)\|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j \\  & =2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+2(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|2t|\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =2t\end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the last step, we removed the absolute value bars since $t>0.$ 

Next, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}2u\,\text{d}u \\  & ={u}^{2}{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & ={t}^{2}-0 \\  & ={t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $s=t^2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =s \\ t & =\pm \sqrt{s} \\ t & =\sqrt{s},\end{aligned}
$$

taking the positive root because $t>0.$  

Finally, the vector function that parametrizes $\mathbf r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{s}) \\  & =2(\sqrt{s}\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s})\,i+2(\sqrt{s}\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}+\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s})\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Consider the curve r(t)=⟨2t,1−3t,5+6t⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=7t. Find R(s), the parametrization of the curve by its arc length s.

a
 R(s)=⟨2s,7−3s,35+6s⟩
b
 R(s)=⟨2s,7+3s,35+6s⟩
c
 R(s)=17⟨2s,7−3s,35+6s⟩
d
 R(s)=17⟨2s,7+3s,35+6s⟩
e
 R(s)=17⟨2s,1−3s,5+6s⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Since s=7t, t=s/7. Substituting gives R(s)=r(s/7)=⟨2s/7,1−3s/7,5+6s/7⟩=(1/7)⟨2s,7−3s,35+6s⟩ for s≥0, which is option c.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=⟨2t,\,1-3t,\,5+6t⟩$, $t\ge 0$, for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=7t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s=7t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{7}.$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s$, with $s\ge 0$, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{7}) \\  & =⟨2(\frac{s}{7}),\,1-3(\frac{s}{7}),\,5+6(\frac{s}{7})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{7}⟨2s,\,7-3s,\,35+6s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 R(s)=⟨2s,7−3s,35+6s⟩
b
 R(s)=⟨2s,7+3s,35+6s⟩
c
 R(s)=17⟨2s,7−3s,35+6s⟩
d
 R(s)=17⟨2s,7+3s,35+6s⟩
e
 R(s)=17⟨2s,1−3s,5+6s⟩
Submit
Correct

content.knowledge_point: Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length Given Its Arc Length
content.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=⟨2t,\,1-3t,\,5+6t⟩$, $t\ge 0$, for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=7t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
content.worked_solution:
First, since $s=7t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{7}.$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s$, with $s\ge 0$, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{7}) \\  & =⟨2(\frac{s}{7}),\,1-3(\frac{s}{7}),\,5+6(\frac{s}{7})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{7}⟨2s,\,7-3s,\,35+6s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the curve r(t)=3ti+2t3/2j+4k, t≥0, for which the arc length from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=2(1+t)3/2−2. Given that R(s) is the parameterization of the given curve by its arc length s, what is the y-component of R?

a
 [(s2+1)3/2−1]3/2
b
 2[(s2+1)2/3−1]3/2
c
 2[(s2+1)1/3−1]3/2
d
 3(s2+1)3/2
e
 2[(s2−1)1/3+1]3/2
Submit

decision.explanation: Solving s=2(1+t)^{3/2}−2 gives t=(s/2+1)^{2/3}−1. Substitute this into the y-component 2t^{3/2} to obtain option b.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=3t\,i+2{t}^{3/2}\,j+4\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by  $s=2(1+t)^{3/2}-2.$ Given that $R(s)$ is the parameterization of the given curve by its arc length $s,$ what is the $y$-component of $R?$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s=2(1+t)^{3/2}-2$, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}s & =2(1+t)^{3/2}-2 \\ s+2 & =2(1+t)^{3/2} \\ \frac{s+2}{2} & =(1+t)^{3/2} \\ {(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3} & =1+t \\ t & ={(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r({(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1) \\  & =3[{(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1]\,i+2{[{(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1]}^{3/2}\,j+4\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the $y$-component of $R$ is

$$
2{[{(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1]}^{3/2}.
$$

Question 2

Consider the curve r(t)=3ti+2t3/2j+4k, t≥0, for which the arc length from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=2(1+t)3/2−2. Given that R(s) is the parameterization of the given curve by its arc length s, what is the y-component of R?

a
 [(s2+1)3/2−1]3/2
b
 2[(s2+1)2/3−1]3/2
c
 2[(s2+1)1/3−1]3/2
d
 3(s2+1)3/2
e
 2[(s2−1)1/3+1]3/2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, since s=2(1+t)3/2−2, we have that s=2(1+t)3/2−2s+2=2(1+t)3/2s+22=(1+t)3/2(s2+1)2/3=1+tt=(s2+1)2/3−1.

Hence, the vector function that parametrizes r(t) by its arc length is given by

R(s)=r((s2+1)2/3−1)=3[(s2+1)2/3−1]i+2[(s2+1)2/3−1]3/2j+4k.

So, the y-component of R is

2[(s2+1)2/3−1]3/2.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option b: invert s=2(1+t)^{3/2}−2 to obtain t=(s/2+1)^{2/3}−1, then substitute into y=2t^{3/2}. The observed incorrect submission selected c, whose inner exponent is 1/3 instead of 2/3.

content.knowledge_point: Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length Given Its Arc Length
content.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=3t\,i+2{t}^{3/2}\,j+4\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by  $s=2(1+t)^{3/2}-2.$ Given that $R(s)$ is the parameterization of the given curve by its arc length $s,$ what is the $y$-component of $R?$
content.worked_solution:
First, since $s=2(1+t)^{3/2}-2$, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}s & =2(1+t)^{3/2}-2 \\ s+2 & =2(1+t)^{3/2} \\ \frac{s+2}{2} & =(1+t)^{3/2} \\ {(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3} & =1+t \\ t & ={(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r({(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1) \\  & =3[{(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1]\,i+2{[{(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1]}^{3/2}\,j+4\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the $y$-component of $R$ is

$$
2{[{(\frac{s}{2}+1)}^{2/3}-1]}^{3/2}.
$$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Consider the curve r(t)=22⟨etsin⁡t,etcos⁡t⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=et−1. Given that R(s) is the parametrization of the given curve by its arc length s, what is the x-component of R?

a
22(s+1)sin⁡[ln⁡(s+1)]
b
(s+1)sin⁡[ln⁡(s)]
c
22(s+1)sin⁡(s+1)
d
s⋅sin⁡[ln⁡(s+1)]
e
22s⋅sin⁡[ln⁡(s)]
Submit

decision.explanation: Since s=e^t−1, e^t=s+1 and t=ln(s+1). Substituting into x(t)=(√2/2)e^t sin(t) gives (√2/2)(s+1)sin[ln(s+1)], which is option a.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s={e}^{t}-1.$ Given that $R(s)$ is the parametrization of the given curve by its arc length $s,$ what is the $x$-component of $R?$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s={e}^{t}-1,$ we have that $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1).$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s,$ with $s\ge 0,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(s+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(s+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the $x$-component of $R$ is

$$
\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(s+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)].
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the curve r(t)=22⟨etsin⁡t,etcos⁡t⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=et−1. Given that R(s) is the parametrization of the given curve by its arc length s, what is the x-component of R?

a
22(s+1)sin⁡[ln⁡(s+1)]
b
(s+1)sin⁡[ln⁡(s)]
c
22(s+1)sin⁡(s+1)
d
s⋅sin⁡[ln⁡(s+1)]
e
22s⋅sin⁡[ln⁡(s)]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, since s=et−1, we have that t=ln⁡(s+1).

The vector function that pametrizes the curve r(t) by its arc length s, with s≥0, is given by R(s)=r(ln⁡(s+1))=22⟨eln⁡(s+1)sin⁡[ln⁡(s+1)],eln⁡(s+1)cos⁡[ln⁡(s+1)]⟩=⟨22(s+1)sin⁡[ln⁡(s+1)],22(s+1)cos⁡[ln⁡(s+1)]⟩.

So, the x-component of R is

22(s+1)sin⁡[ln⁡(s+1)].

content.knowledge_point: Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length Given Its Arc Length
content.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s={e}^{t}-1.$ Given that $R(s)$ is the parametrization of the given curve by its arc length $s,$ what is the $x$-component of $R?$
content.worked_solution:
First, since $s={e}^{t}-1,$ we have that $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1).$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s,$ with $s\ge 0,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(s+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(s+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, the $x$-component of $R$ is

$$
\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(s+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)].
$$

before.html:
Question 4
?

Consider the curve r(t)=⟨1−2cos⁡3t,3−2sin⁡3t⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=6t. Find R(s), the parametrization of the curve by its arc length s.

a
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(s2),3−2sin⁡(s2)⟩
b
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(2s),3−2sin⁡(2s)⟩
c
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(3s−6),3−2sin⁡(3s−6)⟩
d
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(s3),3−2sin⁡(s3)⟩
e
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(3s+2),3−2sin⁡(3s+2)⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Since s=6t, t=s/6 and 3t=s/2. Substitution gives R(s)=⟨1−2cos(s/2),3−2sin(s/2)⟩ for s≥0, matching option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=6t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s=6t,$ we have that $t=\frac{s}{6}.$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s,$ with $s\ge 0,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{6}) \\  & =⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{s}{6}),\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{s}{6})⟩ \\  & =⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Consider the curve r(t)=⟨1−2cos⁡3t,3−2sin⁡3t⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=6t. Find R(s), the parametrization of the curve by its arc length s.

a
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(s2),3−2sin⁡(s2)⟩
b
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(2s),3−2sin⁡(2s)⟩
c
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(3s−6),3−2sin⁡(3s−6)⟩
d
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(s3),3−2sin⁡(s3)⟩
e
R(s)=⟨1−2cos⁡(3s+2),3−2sin⁡(3s+2)⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, since s=6t, we have that t=s6.

The vector function that pametrizes the curve r(t) by its arc length s, with s≥0, is given by R(s)=r(s6)=⟨1−2cos⁡(3⋅s6),3−2sin⁡(3⋅s6)⟩=⟨1−2cos⁡(s2),3−2sin⁡(s2)⟩.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms a: s=6t implies t=s/6, so 3t=s/2. Thus R(s)=r(s/6) has the displayed components in option a and unit speed. The deliberately submitted option c is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length Given Its Arc Length
content.problem: Consider the curve $r(t)=⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=6t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
content.worked_solution:
First, since $s=6t,$ we have that $t=\frac{s}{6}.$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s,$ with $s\ge 0,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{6}) \\  & =⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{s}{6}),\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{s}{6})⟩ \\  & =⟨1-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}),\,3-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

Consider the curver(t)=(1+2sin⁡(2t))i+(2−2cos⁡(2t))j, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=4t. Find R(s), the parametrization of the curve by its arc length s.

a
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(8s))i+(2−2cos⁡(8s))j
b
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(2s))i+(2−2cos⁡(2s))j
c
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(s2))i+(2+2cos⁡(s2))j
d
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(s2))i+(2−2cos⁡(s2))j
e
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(s4))i+(2−2cos⁡(s4))j
Submit

decision.explanation: Since s=4t, t=s/4, so 2t=s/2. Substituting into r(t) gives option d for s≥0.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Consider the curve$r(t)=(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))\,i+(2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))\,j,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by  $s=4t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s=4t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{4}.$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s$, with $s\ge 0$, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{4}) \\  & =(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{s}{4}))\,i+(2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{s}{4}))\,j \\  & =(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))\,i+(2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

a
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(8s))i+(2−2cos⁡(8s))j
b
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(2s))i+(2−2cos⁡(2s))j
c
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(s2))i+(2+2cos⁡(s2))j
d
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(s2))i+(2−2cos⁡(s2))j
e
 R(s)=(1+2sin⁡(s4))i+(2−2cos⁡(s4))j
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, since s=4t, we have that t=s4.

The vector function that pametrizes the curve r(t) by its arc length s, with s≥0, is given by

R(s)=r(s4)=(1+2sin⁡(2⋅s4))i+(2−2cos⁡(2⋅s4))j=(1+2sin⁡(s2))i+(2−2cos⁡(s2))j.

content.knowledge_point: Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length Given Its Arc Length
content.problem: Consider the curve$r(t)=(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))\,i+(2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))\,j,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by  $s=4t.$ Find $R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$
content.worked_solution:
First, since $s=4t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{4}.$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $r(t)$ by its arc length $s$, with $s\ge 0$, is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{4}) \\  & =(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{s}{4}))\,i+(2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{s}{4}))\,j \\  & =(1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))\,i+(2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=⟨2{e}^{t},\,3{e}^{t},\,6{e}^{t}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=7({e}^{t}-1),$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s=7({e}^{t}-1)$, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{s}{7} & ={e}^{t}-1 \\ {e}^{t} & =\frac{s}{7}+1 \\ t & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7}).\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})) \\  & =⟨2{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})},\,3{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})},\,6{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})}⟩ \\  & =⟨2\cdot \frac{s+7}{7},\,3\cdot \frac{s+7}{7},\,6\cdot \frac{s+7}{7}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2s+14}{7},\,\frac{3s+21}{7},\,\frac{6s+42}{7}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2s+14}{7}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3s+21}{7}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{6s+42}{7})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{7},\,\frac{3}{7},\,\frac{6}{7}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Given the curve r(t)=⟨2et,3et,6et⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=7(et−1), find the corresponding unit tangent T(s), parametrized by s.

a
⟨27,37,67⟩
b
⟨25,35,65⟩
c
⟨17,27,37⟩
d
⟨15,35,35⟩
e
⟨214,314,27⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, since s=7(et−1), we have that s7=et−1et=s7+1t=ln⁡(s+77).

Therefore, the vector function R(s) that parametrizes r(t) by its arc length is given by

R(s)=r(ln⁡(s+77))=⟨2eln⁡(s+77),3eln⁡(s+77),6eln⁡(s+77)⟩=⟨2⋅s+77,3⋅s+77,6⋅s+77⟩=⟨2s+147,3s+217,6s+427⟩.

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length s, the unit tangent can be found as T(s)=ddsR(s).

So, we obtain

T(s)=ddsR(s)=⟨dds(2s+147),dds(3s+217),dds(6s+427)⟩=⟨27,37,67⟩.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Unit Tangent Given the Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length
content.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=⟨2{e}^{t},\,3{e}^{t},\,6{e}^{t}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=7({e}^{t}-1),$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
content.worked_solution:
First, since $s=7({e}^{t}-1)$, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{s}{7} & ={e}^{t}-1 \\ {e}^{t} & =\frac{s}{7}+1 \\ t & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7}).\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})) \\  & =⟨2{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})},\,3{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})},\,6{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{s+7}{7})}⟩ \\  & =⟨2\cdot \frac{s+7}{7},\,3\cdot \frac{s+7}{7},\,6\cdot \frac{s+7}{7}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2s+14}{7},\,\frac{3s+21}{7},\,\frac{6s+42}{7}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2s+14}{7}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3s+21}{7}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{6s+42}{7})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{7},\,\frac{3}{7},\,\frac{6}{7}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 7
?

Given the curve r(t)=8cos⁡ti+8sin⁡tj+6tk, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=10t, find the corresponding unit tangent T(s), parametrized by s.

a
T(s)=−45sin⁡(s10)i+45cos⁡(s10)j+35k
b
T(s)=45sin⁡(s10)i−45cos⁡(s10)j+35k
c
T(s)=−80sin⁡(s10)i+80cos⁡(s10)j+35k
d
T(s)=−45sin⁡(10s)i+45cos⁡(10s)j+35k
e
T(s)=80sin⁡(s10)i−80cos⁡(s10)j+35k
Submit

decision.explanation: Since s=10t, substitute t=s/10 into r(t) and differentiate with respect to s. This gives T(s)=−(4/5)sin(s/10)i+(4/5)cos(s/10)j+(3/5)k, matching option a. Its squared norm is 16/25+9/25=1.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+6t\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=10t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s=10t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{10}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{10}) \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})i+8\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})j+6(\frac{s}{10})k \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})i+8\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})j+\frac{3s}{5}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(8\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{10})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(8\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{10})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3s}{5})k \\  & =-8\cdot \frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})i+8\cdot \frac{1}{10}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})j+\frac{3}{5}\,k \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})i+\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})j+\frac{3}{5}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Given the curve r(t)=8cos⁡ti+8sin⁡tj+6tk, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=10t, find the corresponding unit tangent T(s), parametrized by s.

a
T(s)=−45sin⁡(s10)i+45cos⁡(s10)j+35k
b
T(s)=45sin⁡(s10)i−45cos⁡(s10)j+35k
c
T(s)=−80sin⁡(s10)i+80cos⁡(s10)j+35k
d
T(s)=−45sin⁡(10s)i+45cos⁡(10s)j+35k
e
T(s)=80sin⁡(s10)i−80cos⁡(s10)j+35k
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, since s=10t, we have that t=s10.

Therefore, the vector function R(s) that parametrizes r(t) by its arc length is given by

R(s)=r(s10)=8cos⁡(s10)i+8sin⁡(s10)j+6(s10)k=8cos⁡(s10)i+8sin⁡(s10)j+3s5k.

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length s, the unit tangent can be found as T(s)=ddsR(s).

So, we obtain

T(s)=ddsR(s)=dds(8cos⁡s10)i+dds(8sin⁡s10)j+dds(3s5)k=−8⋅110sin⁡(s10)i+8⋅110cos⁡(s10)j+35k=−45sin⁡(s10)i+45cos⁡(s10)j+35k.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a. With t=s/10, differentiating R(s)=r(s/10) introduces a factor of 1/10, giving coefficients −4/5, 4/5, and 3/5. The resulting vector has norm 1; the deliberately submitted option c does not.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Unit Tangent Given the Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length
content.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+6t\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=10t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
content.worked_solution:
First, since $s=10t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{10}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{10}) \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})i+8\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})j+6(\frac{s}{10})k \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})i+8\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})j+\frac{3s}{5}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(8\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{10})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(8\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{10})j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3s}{5})k \\  & =-8\cdot \frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})i+8\cdot \frac{1}{10}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})j+\frac{3}{5}\,k \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})i+\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})j+\frac{3}{5}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

T(s)=−80sin⁡(s10)i+80cos⁡(s10)j+35k

Question 8
?

Given the curve r(t)=8ti+cos⁡6tj+sin⁡6tk, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=10t, find the corresponding unit tangent T(s), parametrized by s.

a
 T(s)=4s5i+35cos⁡(3s5)j+sin⁡(3s5)k
b
 T(s)=4s5i+cos⁡(3s5)j+sin⁡(3s5)k
c
 T(s)=35i+35sin⁡(3s5)j+35cos⁡(3s5)k
d
 T(s)=45i−35sin⁡(3s5)j+35cos⁡(3s5)k
e
 T(s)=2s5i+cos⁡(3s5)j+sin⁡(3s5)k
Submit

decision.explanation: Since t=s/10, R(s)=(4s/5)i+cos(3s/5)j+sin(3s/5)k. Differentiating gives T(s)=(4/5)i−(3/5)sin(3s/5)j+(3/5)cos(3s/5)k, which has norm 1 and matches option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=8t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡6t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡6t\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=10t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s=10t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{10}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{10}) \\  & =8(\frac{s}{10})\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{6s}{10})j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{6s}{10})k \\  & =\frac{4s}{5}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4s}{5})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5}))j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5}))k \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})j+\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})k.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Given the curve r(t)=8ti+cos⁡6tj+sin⁡6tk, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=10t, find the corresponding unit tangent T(s), parametrized by s.

a
 T(s)=4s5i+35cos⁡(3s5)j+sin⁡(3s5)k
b
 T(s)=4s5i+cos⁡(3s5)j+sin⁡(3s5)k
c
 T(s)=35i+35sin⁡(3s5)j+35cos⁡(3s5)k
d
 T(s)=45i−35sin⁡(3s5)j+35cos⁡(3s5)k
e
 T(s)=2s5i+cos⁡(3s5)j+sin⁡(3s5)k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, since s=10t, we have that t=s10.

Therefore, the vector function R(s) that parametrizes r(t) by its arc length is given by

R(s)=r(s10)=8(s10)i+cos⁡(6s10)j+sin⁡(6s10)k=4s5i+cos⁡(3s5)j+sin⁡(3s5)k.

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length s, the unit tangent can be found as T(s)=ddsR(s).

So, we obtain T(s)=ddsR(s)=dds(4s5)i+dds(cos⁡(3s5))j+dds(sin⁡(3s5))k=45i−35sin⁡(3s5)j+35cos⁡(3s5)k.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Unit Tangent Given the Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length
content.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=8t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡6t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡6t\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=10t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
content.worked_solution:
First, since $s=10t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{10}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{10}) \\  & =8(\frac{s}{10})\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{6s}{10})j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{6s}{10})k \\  & =\frac{4s}{5}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4s}{5})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5}))j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5}))k \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})j+\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})k.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Given the curve r(t)=⟨t2,4t2,8t2⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=9t2, find the corresponding unit tangent T(s), parametrized by s.

a
⟨181,481,881⟩
b
⟨19,29,13⟩
c
⟨19,29,229⟩
d
⟨19,49,89⟩
e
⟨118,29,49⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Since s=9t², t²=s/9. Thus R(s)=⟨s/9,4s/9,8s/9⟩, and T(s)=R′(s)=⟨1/9,4/9,8/9⟩. Its norm is √(1+16+64)/9=1, confirming option d.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,4{t}^{2},\,8{t}^{2}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=9{t}^{2},$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s=9{t}^{2}$, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{s}{9} \\ t & =\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3}) \\  & =⟨{(\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3})}^{2},\,4{(\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3})}^{2},\,8{(\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3})}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{s}{9},\,\frac{4s}{9},\,\frac{8s}{9}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{9}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4s}{9}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{8s}{9})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{9},\,\frac{4}{9},\,\frac{8}{9}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

Given the curve r(t)=⟨t2,4t2,8t2⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=9t2, find the corresponding unit tangent T(s), parametrized by s.

a
⟨181,481,881⟩
b
⟨19,29,13⟩
c
⟨19,29,229⟩
d
⟨19,49,89⟩
e
⟨118,29,49⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, since s=9t2, we have that t2=s9t=s3.

Therefore, the vector function R(s) that parametrizes r(t) by its arc length is given by

R(s)=r(s3)=⟨(s3)2,4(s3)2,8(s3)2⟩=⟨s9,4s9,8s9⟩.

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length s, the unit tangent can be found as T(s)=ddsR(s).

So, we obtain

T(s)=ddsR(s)=⟨dds(s9),dds(4s9),dds(8s9)⟩=⟨19,49,89⟩.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option d: t²=s/9 gives R(s)=⟨s/9,4s/9,8s/9⟩, so T(s)=R′(s)=⟨1/9,4/9,8/9⟩. Its norm is √81/9=1. The deliberately submitted option c is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Unit Tangent Given the Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length
content.problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,4{t}^{2},\,8{t}^{2}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=9{t}^{2},$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
content.worked_solution:
First, since $s=9{t}^{2}$, we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{s}{9} \\ t & =\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3}) \\  & =⟨{(\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3})}^{2},\,4{(\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3})}^{2},\,8{(\frac{\sqrt{s}}{3})}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{s}{9},\,\frac{4s}{9},\,\frac{8s}{9}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{9}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4s}{9}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{8s}{9})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{9},\,\frac{4}{9},\,\frac{8}{9}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Given the curve r(t)=55⟨t2,−2t2,−2⟩, t≥0, for which the arc length s from r(0) to r(t) is given by s=t2, find the corresponding unit tangent T(s), parametrized by s.

a
T(s)=66⟨1,−1,−2⟩
b
T(s)=13⟨1,−2,2⟩
c
T(s)=13⟨2,−1,−2⟩
d
T(s)=−55⟨1,0,2⟩
e
T(s)=55⟨1,−2,0⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Since t²=s, R(s)=(√5/5)⟨s,−2s,−2⟩. Differentiating gives T(s)=(√5/5)⟨1,−2,0⟩, whose norm is 1. This matches option e.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨{t}^{2},\,-2{t}^{2},\,-2⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s={t}^{2},$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
after.worked_solution:
First, since $s={t}^{2},$ we have that $t=\sqrt{s}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{s}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨{(\sqrt{s})}^{2},\,-2{(\sqrt{s})}^{2},\,-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨s,\,-2s,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parameterized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-2s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-2)⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨1,\,-2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{s}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨{(\sqrt{s})}^{2},\,-2{(\sqrt{s})}^{2},\,-2⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨s,\,-2s,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, since the curve is parameterized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-2s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-2)⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}⟨1,\,-2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

What is the parametrization of the curve r(t)=⟨t4,12t4+2,3−t4⟩, t≥0, by its arc length s?

a
R(s)=13⟨2s,s+6,9−2s⟩
b
R(s)=14⟨2s,3s,2−3s⟩
c
R(s)=13⟨s,2s−3,−2s⟩
d
R(s)=13⟨s,2s+3,2s−3⟩
e
R(s)=14⟨3s,s,1−6s⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: r′(t)=⟨4t³,2t³,−4t³⟩ has magnitude 6t³ for t≥0. Hence s=∫₀ᵗ6u³ du=(3/2)t⁴, so t⁴=2s/3. Substitution gives R(s)=(1/3)⟨2s,s+6,9−2s⟩ for s≥0, matching option a.

after.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}+2,\,3-{t}^{4}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}+2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-{t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2{t}^{3},\,-4{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =2{t}^{3}⟨2,\,1,\,-2⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|2{t}^{3}|\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =2{t}^{3}\sqrt{4+1+4} \\  & =6{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}6{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{t}{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{u}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4}$ and $t\ge 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4} & =s \\ {t}^{4} & =\frac{2s}{3} \\ t & =\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}}) \\  & =⟨{(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}})}^{4},\,\frac{1}{2}{(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}})}^{4}+2,\,3-{(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}})}^{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2s}{3},\,\frac{s}{3}+2,\,3-\frac{2s}{3}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2s,\,s+6,\,9-2s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

What is the parametrization of the curve r(t)=⟨t4,12t4+2,3−t4⟩, t≥0, by its arc length s?

a
R(s)=13⟨2s,s+6,9−2s⟩
b
R(s)=14⟨2s,3s,2−3s⟩
c
R(s)=13⟨s,2s−3,−2s⟩
d
R(s)=13⟨s,2s+3,2s−3⟩
e
R(s)=14⟨3s,s,1−6s⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find r′(t) and its magnitude ‖r′(t)‖: r′(t)=⟨ddt(t4),ddt(12t4+2),ddt(3−t4)⟩=⟨4t3,2t3,−4t3⟩=2t3⟨2,1,−2⟩‖r′(t)‖=|2t3|(2)2+(1)2+(−2)2=2t34+1+4=6t3

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from 0 to t: s=∫0t‖r′(u)‖du=∫0t6u3du=6∫0tu3du=32u4|0t=32t4

content.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{4},\,\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}+2,\,3-{t}^{4}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}+2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-{t}^{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3},\,2{t}^{3},\,-4{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =2{t}^{3}⟨2,\,1,\,-2⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|2{t}^{3}|\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =2{t}^{3}\sqrt{4+1+4} \\  & =6{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}6{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =6{\int }_{0}^{t}{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{u}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4}$ and $t\ge 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{t}^{4} & =s \\ {t}^{4} & =\frac{2s}{3} \\ t & =\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}}) \\  & =⟨{(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}})}^{4},\,\frac{1}{2}{(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}})}^{4}+2,\,3-{(\sqrt[4]{\frac{2s}{3}})}^{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2s}{3},\,\frac{s}{3}+2,\,3-\frac{2s}{3}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2s,\,s+6,\,9-2s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

a
sin⁡(s4)i+cos⁡(s4)j
b
cos4⁡(s)i+sin4⁡(s)j
c
cos⁡(s)i+sin⁡(s)j

−sin⁡(s)i+cos⁡(s)j

decision.explanation: The derivative is r′(t)=4t³⟨−sin(t⁴),cos(t⁴)⟩, whose magnitude is 4t³ for t≥0. Thus s=∫₀ᵗ4u³ du=t⁴. Substituting t⁴=s gives R(s)=cos(s)i+sin(s)j for s≥0, matching option c.

after.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4})\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4})\,j,$  $\,t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4}))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4}))j \\  & =-4{t}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4})\,i+4{t}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4})\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{[-4{t}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4})]}^{2}+{[4{t}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4})]}^{2}} \\  & =4|t{|}^{3}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{4})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{4})} \\  & =4{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}4{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={u}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & ={t}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

  

Now, since $s={t}^{4}$, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{4} & =s \\ t & =\sqrt[4]{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt[4]{s}) \\  & =cos\,((\sqrt[4]{s})^{4})\,i+sin\,((\sqrt[4]{s})^{4})\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(s)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(s)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Next, we calculate the arc length of the curve from 0 to t:

s=∫0t‖r′(u)‖du=∫0t4u3du=u4|0t=t4

Now, since s=t4, we have that t4=st=s4.

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes r(t) by its arc length is given by

R(s)=r(s4)=cos((s4)4)i+sin((s4)4)j=cos⁡(s)i+sin⁡(s)j.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length
content.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4})\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4})\,j,$  $\,t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4}))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4}))j \\  & =-4{t}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4})\,i+4{t}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4})\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{[-4{t}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{4})]}^{2}+{[4{t}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{4})]}^{2}} \\  & =4|t{|}^{3}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{4})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{4})} \\  & =4{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}4{u}^{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={u}^{4}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & ={t}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

  

Now, since $s={t}^{4}$, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{4} & =s \\ t & =\sqrt[4]{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt[4]{s}) \\  & =cos\,((\sqrt[4]{s})^{4})\,i+sin\,((\sqrt[4]{s})^{4})\,j \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(s)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(s)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

What is the parametrization of the curve r(t)=⟨t2,t2,t⟩, t≥0, by its arc length s?

a
R(s)=⟨3s2,3s6,3s6⟩
b
R(s)=⟨6s4,6s4,6s8⟩
c
R(s)=⟨6s6,6s6,6s3⟩
d
R(s)=⟨6s3,6s3,6s8⟩
e
R(s)=⟨3s6,3s6,3s3⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: The speed is ‖r′(t)‖=√(1/4+1/4+1)=√6/2. Thus s=(√6/2)t and t=√6 s/3. Substitution gives R(s)=⟨√6 s/6,√6 s/6,√6 s/3⟩ for s≥0, matching option c.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨\frac{t}{2},\,\frac{t}{2},\,t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2},\,\frac{1}{2},\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\cdot u{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\,t\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\,t$,  we have that $t=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s.$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s,\,\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s,\,\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{6}\,s}{6},\,\frac{\sqrt{6}\,s}{6},\,\frac{\sqrt{6}\,s}{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

What is the parametrization of the curve r(t)=⟨t2,t2,t⟩, t≥0, by its arc length s?

a
R(s)=⟨3s2,3s6,3s6⟩
b
R(s)=⟨6s4,6s4,6s8⟩
c
R(s)=⟨6s6,6s6,6s3⟩
d
R(s)=⟨6s3,6s3,6s8⟩
e
R(s)=⟨3s6,3s6,3s3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find r′(t) and its magnitude ‖r′(t)‖:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(t2),ddt(t2),ddt(t)⟩=⟨12,12,1⟩‖r′(t)‖=(12)2+(12)2+12=14+14+1=32

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from 0 to t: s=∫0t‖r′(u)‖du=∫0t32du=32⋅u|0t=32t Since s=32t, we have that t=23s.

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes r(t) by its arc length is given by

R(s)=r(23s)=⟨12⋅23s,12⋅23s,23s⟩=⟨6s6,6s6,6s3⟩.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length
content.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨\frac{t}{2},\,\frac{t}{2},\,t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{t}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2},\,\frac{1}{2},\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\cdot u{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\,t\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\,t$,  we have that $t=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s.$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s) \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s,\,\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s,\,\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\,s⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{6}\,s}{6},\,\frac{\sqrt{6}\,s}{6},\,\frac{\sqrt{6}\,s}{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 14
?

What is the parametrization of the curve r(t)=⟨tsin⁡t+cos⁡t,3,tcos⁡t−sin⁡t⟩, t≥0, by its arc length s?

a
R(s)=⟨2scos⁡2s,3,−2ssin⁡2s⟩
b
R(s)=⟨2ssin⁡2s+cos⁡2s,3,2scos⁡2s−sin⁡2s⟩
c
R(s)=⟨s2sin⁡(s2)+cos⁡(s2),3,s2cos⁡(s2)−sin⁡(s2)⟩
d
R(s)=⟨2ssin⁡2s+cos⁡2s,3,2scos⁡2s−sin⁡2s⟩
e
R(s)=⟨2scos⁡2s,3,−2ssin⁡2s⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives r′(t)=⟨t cos(t),0,−t sin(t)⟩, so the speed is t for t≥0. Therefore s=∫₀ᵗu du=t²/2 and t=√(2s). Substituting into r(t) gives option d.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3,\,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t+{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}} \\  & =|t| \\  & =t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=\frac{{t}^{2}}{2},$ we have that $t=\sqrt{2s}.$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{2s}) \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2s}\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}+\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s},\,3,\,\sqrt{2s}\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s}-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametrization of a Curve by Arc Length
content.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3,\,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t+{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}} \\  & =|t| \\  & =t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=\frac{{t}^{2}}{2},$ we have that $t=\sqrt{2s}.$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{2s}) \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2s}\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}+\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s},\,3,\,\sqrt{2s}\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s}-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 15
?

What is the parametrization of the curve r(t)=12⟨−etcos⁡t,etsin⁡t⟩, t≥0, by its arc length s?

a
R(s)=s+12⟨−cos⁡(s+1),sin⁡(s+1)⟩
b
R(s)=s2⟨−cos⁡(ln⁡s),sin⁡(ln⁡s)⟩
c
R(s)=s+12⟨−cos⁡(ln⁡s),sin⁡(ln⁡s)⟩
d
R(s)=s+12⟨−cos⁡[ln⁡(s+1)],sin⁡[ln⁡(s+1)]⟩
e
R(s)=s2⟨−cos⁡[ln⁡(s−1)],sin⁡[ln⁡(s−1)]⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: The derivative is (e^t/√2)⟨sin(t)−cos(t),sin(t)+cos(t)⟩, whose magnitude is e^t. Thus s=∫₀ᵗe^u du=e^t−1, giving t=ln(s+1) and e^t=s+1. Substitution into r(t) yields option d for s≥0.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t-{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}|\sqrt{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & ={e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={e}^{u}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & ={e}^{t}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s={e}^{t}-1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{t}-1 & =s \\ {e}^{t} & =s+1 \\ t & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-(s+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,(s+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩ \\  & =\frac{s+1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

What is the parametrization of the curve r(t)=12⟨−etcos⁡t,etsin⁡t⟩, t≥0, by its arc length s?

a
R(s)=s+12⟨−cos⁡(s+1),sin⁡(s+1)⟩
b
R(s)=s2⟨−cos⁡(ln⁡s),sin⁡(ln⁡s)⟩
c
R(s)=s+12⟨−cos⁡(ln⁡s),sin⁡(ln⁡s)⟩
d
R(s)=s+12⟨−cos⁡[ln⁡(s+1)],sin⁡[ln⁡(s+1)]⟩
e
R(s)=s2⟨−cos⁡[ln⁡(s−1)],sin⁡[ln⁡(s−1)]⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find r′(t) and its magnitude ‖r′(t)‖: r′(t)=12⟨ddt(−etcos⁡t),ddt(etsin⁡t)⟩=12⟨etsin⁡t−etcos⁡t,etsin⁡t+etcos⁡t⟩=et2⟨sin⁡t−cos⁡t,sin⁡t+cos⁡t⟩‖r′(t)‖=|et2|(sin⁡t−cos⁡t)2+(sin⁡t+cos⁡t)2=et2sin2⁡t−2sin⁡tcos⁡t+cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t+2sin⁡tcos⁡t+cos2⁡t=et22(sin2⁡t+cos2⁡t)=et2⋅2=et

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from 0 to t: s=∫0t‖r′(u)‖du=∫0teudu=eu|0t=et−1

Since s=et−1, we have et−1=set=s+1t=ln⁡(s+1).

content.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t-{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}|\sqrt{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & ={e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={e}^{u}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & ={e}^{t}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s={e}^{t}-1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{t}-1 & =s \\ {e}^{t} & =s+1 \\ t & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)}\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-(s+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,(s+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩ \\  & =\frac{s+1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)],\,\operatorname{sin}⁡[\operatorname{ln}⁡(s+1)]⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
